versions.changelog:
## OpenWatchParty v0.7.0

A security and feature release for the session server and Jellyfin 12 plugin.

### Security update

Upgrade the **session server** to 0.7.0. Earlier releases, from 0.1.0 through 0.6.0, can reflect oversized application pings into queued pong responses before authentication. The fix constructs a bounded response containing only a validated clock-sync timestamp. This addresses GHSA-fjpr-3g28-27r9.

This release also enforces the inviter bookkeeping cap and makes per-IP permit acquisition and cleanup race-safe. Thanks to **@francotosqui** for reporting privately, reviewing the fix and contributing both hardening changes.

**Updating only the Jellyfin plugin does not fix an older session server.** Retain the plugin version compatible with your Jellyfin installation; the server update is a separate component. The v0.7.0 plugin targets Jellyfin 12.0/12.1, not Jellyfin 10.11.

### Highlights

- Host-controlled room queues of up to 20 items, episode autofill, synchronized advancement and cancellable up-next countdowns.
- Configurable opacity and text size, including proportional controls and reduced-transparency support.
- Watch Party controls in the player's header next to Cast.
- Shared guest play/pause controls, host transfer and reconnect recovery.
- Participant status, manual guest synchronization adjustment, first-run help and localized UI strings.
- Lower idle client overhead, bounded rendered chat, fewer unnecessary room-list broadcasts and in-memory index injection.
- Prometheus metrics, readiness checks, fuzz coverage and expanded lifecycle/browser regressions.
- TLS dependency updates and refreshed Alpine runtime packages.

### Compatibility and upgrade

- WebSocket protocol remains **1**; Rust MSRV remains **1.88**.
- Jellyfin plugin target ABI remains **12.0.0.0**; development testing uses Jellyfin **12.1**.
- Plugin automatic updates remain disabled by default pending the official publication and upgrade-path checks. Existing operator preferences are not overwritten.
- Restarting the session server clears its in-memory rooms. Schedule the update outside an active watch party.

Use `ghcr.io/mhbxyz/owp-session-server:0.7.0` for a version-pinned server deployment. Download `OpenWatchParty-v0.7.0.zip` for the Jellyfin 12 plugin, or use the compatible entry in the plugin repository once the manifest update completes.

### Validation and supply chain

The combined fix passed 315 server tests on Rust 1.88, 651 client tests, 164 .NET tests, 39 CLI tests and 18 browser E2E tests on an isolated JWT-authenticated Jellyfin 12.1/Chrome stack. Cargo audits, formatting, Clippy, client/fuzz contracts and release-script checks passed. Queue-size regressions are not a live RSS/OOM benchmark.

The release workflow builds versioned amd64/arm64 server images and CLI binaries for Linux, macOS and Windows. Downloadable assets and their checksums, signatures, attestations and SBOMs are attached as the workflow completes.

[Full changelog](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/blob/v0.7.0/CHANGELOG.md) · [Installation](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/blob/v0.7.0/docs/operations/installation.md) · [Security advisory](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/security/advisories/GHSA-fjpr-3g28-27r9)

## Highlights

- **Room invite links**: the host can copy a room-scoped, expiring link; a guest who opens it lands in Jellyfin Web and joins the room automatically after signing in ([#66](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/issues/66), [#76](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/76)).
- **Protocol versioning**: clients declare their protocol version in the auth exchange; a missing field defaults to version `1` and an unsupported one is rejected with `PROTOCOL_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED` ([#61](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/issues/61), [#75](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/75)).
- **A dedicated Watch Party icon** in the header, the player OSD and the cards, distinct from Jellyfin's SyncPlay button ([#81](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/81)).
- **Keyboard and screen-reader support for the panel**: `role="dialog"`, focus entry and restore, Escape handling, `aria-expanded` synchronisation and accessible drop-downs ([#82](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/82)).
- **Home card fix**: joining from a card now plays that card's media instead of the first play button found in the document ([#78](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/78)).
- **Header observer scoped** to actual header changes, so library pages no longer trigger per-frame lookups ([#79](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/79)).

## Operations

- **owpctl**: new `logs` command and `doctor --bundle` (redacted support bundle); release artifacts now cover Linux x86_64/arm64, macOS arm64/x86_64 and Windows x86_64, signed and attested ([#64](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/issues/64), [#74](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/74)).
- **Security documentation**: technical threat model and abuse-limits inventory ([#67](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/issues/67), [#77](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/77)), and a deployment warning for caches that ignore query strings ([#57](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/issues/57), [#80](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/80)).
- **Testing**: two-user Playwright end-to-end suite covering joins, playback sync, the paused-room hold, leaving, reconnection and the home card ([#60](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/issues/60), [#73](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/73)); the local `just test plugin` recipe now works after a plugin build.
- Documentation and screenshots were refreshed for the v0.5.0 UI earlier in this cycle ([#55](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/issues/55), [#58](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/58)).

## Validation

Client (335 tests), plugin (144 on .NET 10), server (220) and owpctl suites pass, together with the release-script suite and the end-to-end suite in CI. The Security workflow is green, and the release image, plugin and owpctl binaries are built, signed and attested by the publish workflow.

## Breaking changes

None. Protocol version `1` is negotiated with backward-compatible defaults, and the invite ticket travels in the existing `join_room` payload.

## Header and SyncPlay controls

- Watch Party button in the Jellyfin header, in both Jellyfin 12 layouts (legacy `.headerRight` and the MUI app bar); the panel opens below the header, follows layout changes and stays reachable inside the player from the OSD button ([#45](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/issues/45), [#48](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/48)).
- New admin setting, off by default: hide Jellyfin's built-in SyncPlay button. The client applies it from both `/Token` response modes, and turning it off restores SyncPlay ([#48](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/48)).
- Joining from the header starts the room's media and syncs to the host; rooms without media are marked "No media" and joining one while nothing plays shows a hint; Create Room stays disabled, with a hint, until something plays ([#48](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/48)).
- `owpctl install` and `configure` now carry over the plugin settings they do not manage, starting with the SyncPlay setting ([#48](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/48)).

## Room experience

- Participant names in the room, in join order, with a separate Host badge. The server sends a new `participant_list` message; older servers keep showing the participant count, and older clients ignore the message ([#49](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/49)).
- The room panel is now a compact bar: sync dot, latency, room name, participants, chat with unread badge, leave and close buttons, each drop-down opening one at a time. Leaving always asks first, and chat counts as read only while it is on screen ([#49](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/49)).
- Rooms are named `<host>'s room` instead of the Spanish-era `Room de <host>`, and the room list panel shares the bar's look ([#49](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/49)).
- The home "Watch Parties" card uses Jellyfin's landscape card markup and follows the active theme ([#49](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/49)).
- Guests can no longer keep playing while the room is paused: the client pauses them within the sync loop and shows "Only the host can control playback" ([#52](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/52)).

## Performance

- The injected loader URL is versioned by the client content hash, and the loader and modules are served `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` for the current hash (`no-store` for any other). After the first visit, a page load makes zero requests for OpenWatchParty files until an update ([#50](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/50)).

## Dependencies and docs

- `rand` 0.10.3 (#51), `ruby/setup-ruby` 1.327 (#47), refreshed Rust and Alpine image digests, and a patched vulnerable `brace-expansion`.
- Docs: header button and native SyncPlay setting, the `participant_list` protocol, room bar and client reference, and the versioned cache policy; the illustrated first watch party walkthrough and GitHub community health files were completed earlier on `main`.

## Validation

Client (282 tests), plugin (139 on .NET 10), server (192) and owpctl suites pass, together with the release-script suite and the version mirrors. The Security workflow (Gitleaks, `cargo audit`, `npm audit`, NuGet audit, `bundle-audit`, Trivy, CodeQL) is green, and the release image and plugin assets are built, signed and attested by the publish workflow.

## Breaking changes

None. `participant_list` is additive, and the new `/Token` field is ignored by older clients.

## Jellyfin 12 support

OpenWatchParty `0.4.0` is the first release for the Jellyfin 12 line. The plugin is compiled against Jellyfin packages `12.0.0`, targets ABI `12.0.0.0` and builds on .NET 10, so it installs on Jellyfin 12.0 and 12.1. It resolves the 401 wall reported in [#33](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/issues/33).

- Send the modern `Authorization: MediaBrowser Token="…"` header from the client and the configuration page. Jellyfin 12 disables legacy authorization, so this is the fix for the 401s.
- Keep the client fixes that shipped in `0.3.4`: retry backoff for blocked authentications and a support report that survives a failed diagnostics run.

## Client

- Back off blocked authentication retries: exponential delay (5 s → 5 min) instead of every 2 seconds, the same error toast is not repeated, and a fresh Jellyfin login retries immediately.
- Keep failed diagnostics in the support report: the report records the diagnostics failure, adds the loader error, page origin and user agent, and keeps the last successful payload.
- Reject WebSocket message types inherited from `Object.prototype` ([#40](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/40)). Message types are resolved as own properties and must be functions before dispatch, closing CodeQL alert [#143](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/security/code-scanning/143) (`js/unvalidated-dynamic-method-call`, CWE-754).

## Server

- Keep WebSocket connections alive with protocol heartbeats.
- Count chat message limits in Unicode characters.
- Stop broadcasting the room list to unauthenticated clients.
- Cache the RSA trust store between token validations.
- Pick up the fixed `libssl3` in the runtime image ([#37](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/37)), which clears the Trivy finding.

## Dependencies

- Server ([#31](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/31)): `tokio` 1.53, `jsonwebtoken` 11 with the `aws_lc_rs` provider, `uuid` 1.26, `serde` 1.0.229, `serde_json` 1.0.151, `futures` 0.3.34, `env_logger` 0.11, `base64` 0.23, `ipnet` 2.12.2, `log` 0.4.34.
- owpctl ([#36](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/36)): `rand` 0.10, `sha2` 0.11, `toml` 1.1, `tungstenite` 0.30, `dirs` 7, `clap` 4.6.7, `base64` 0.23, `uuid` 1.26.
- Docker ([#22](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/22)): build on Rust `1.98-alpine`, run on `alpine:3.24`.
- GitHub Actions ([#38](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/38)): 16 actions bumped to their current major versions.
- Documentation ([#39](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/39)): Jekyll 4.4.1.
- Repository: Dependabot vulnerability alerts and security updates are enabled, alongside the existing CodeQL, Gitleaks and audit jobs ([#42](https://github.com/mhbxyz/OpenWatchParty/pull/42)).

## Breaking changes

- OpenWatchParty `0.4.0` targets Jellyfin 12. Installations on Jellyfin 10.11 must stay on `0.3.4`; both lines are published from the same plugin repository manifest.

## Validation

Server (187 tests), owpctl (26 tests), plugin (113 tests on .NET 10) and client (181 tests) suites pass, together with the release-script suite and `verify-versions.sh`. The Security workflow (Gitleaks, `cargo audit`, `npm audit`, NuGet audit, `bundle-audit`, Trivy, CodeQL) is green, and the release image builds and smoke-tests on Alpine 3.24.

## Client fixes for the Jellyfin 10.11 line

This patch brings the client fixes from the Jellyfin 12 work to installations that stay on Jellyfin 10.11. It keeps the `10.11.0.0` target ABI, so it installs alongside the existing 10.11 versions from the same plugin repository.

### Fixed

- Send the modern `Authorization: MediaBrowser Token="…"` header from the client and the configuration page. Jellyfin 10.11 also accepts it, and it is required when legacy authorization is disabled.
- Back off blocked authentication retries: a rejected token is retried with exponential delay (5 s → 5 min) instead of every 2 seconds, the same error toast is not repeated, and a fresh Jellyfin login still retries immediately.
- Keep failed diagnostics in the support report: the report records that diagnostics failed, adds the loader error, page origin and user agent, and keeps the last successful payload.

### Validation

Client (175 tests), plugin (113 tests on `net9.0`) and Rust (server + owpctl) suites pass, together with `verify-versions.sh` and the release-script suite, against the `10.11.0.0` target ABI.

## Reliability and security hardening

- Trust stores are mounted by directory so atomic key rotation and revocation are immediately visible inside Docker.
- Unknown JWT authentication modes now fail closed at startup.
- Jellyfin base paths are preserved by owpctl API requests.
- Upgrading an adopted plugin no longer claims ownership for uninstall.
- Installation persists recoverable ownership state before external mutations.
- Configuration and JWT rotation attempt automatic rollback across plugin, files and Compose.
- The graphical wizard keeps Jellyfin admin tokens in memory only.

## Validation

All server, plugin, client and owpctl suites pass. The installer completed real install, authenticated doctor, RS256 pairing, asymmetric restart, backup and ownership-safe uninstall against Jellyfin 10.11.3.

## owpctl usability fix

- Changing `session.published-port` now automatically updates the managed public WebSocket URL when it still points to the previous managed port.

## Validation

Verified with the signed release installer flow, isolated session-server port configuration, Jellyfin plugin upgrade, authenticated doctor, RS256 pairing, asymmetric restart, backup and ownership-safe uninstall.

## owpctl fixes

- Upgrade now compares and installs the requested plugin version instead of treating any existing plugin as current.
- `session.published-port` can be configured before install, enabling isolated and multi-instance deployments.

## Validation

The release candidate completed a real setup/install/doctor workflow against Jellyfin 10.11.3, then paired RS256, restarted in asymmetric mode, passed authenticated WebSocket ping/pong, created a backup and completed ownership-safe uninstall.

## Guided installation

- New signed `owpctl` installer with CLI and loopback-only graphical setup wizard.
- Automated Jellyfin repository/plugin installation, session-server deployment, synchronized configuration, health verification, upgrade, backup and uninstall.
- `owpctl doctor` performs authenticated plugin and WebSocket ping/pong diagnostics.

## Administration

- New Jellyfin health dashboard with active session diagnostics, injection counters, version compatibility and redacted support reports.
- Advanced settings are collapsed; secure secret generation and pairing status are integrated.

## Authentication

- RS256 plugin signing keys remain private in Jellyfin.
- Versioned public-key trust store with strict `kid`/algorithm validation.
- Explicit `hs256`, `hybrid` and `asymmetric` server modes.
- `owpctl pair` migrates managed deployments from hybrid to asymmetric mode without copying private keys.

## Documentation

Installation, development and usage paths are now separated. `just up` is documented as development-only.

## E2E fixes

- Bind browser timer methods correctly to prevent Chrome `Illegal invocation` after authentication.
- Retry OpenWatchParty connection automatically after a Jellyfin SPA login.
- Launch guest media through the official Jellyfin details/play flow when Jellyfin 10.11 does not expose `playbackManager`.

## Validation

Tested with two isolated Jellyfin users on Spider-Man (2002): room creation/join, automatic guest playback, seek propagation, pause/resume, and clock-corrected synchronization within single-digit milliseconds.

## Highlights

- Reliable synchronized playback with atomic room state, monotonic scheduling, reconnection recovery, and media-correlated readiness.
- Hardened JWT authentication, WebSocket validation, resource limits, backpressure handling, and graceful shutdown.
- Jellyfin 10.11-compatible plugin injection with embedded modular client assets and deterministic packaging.
- Reproducible, signed supply chain with locked dependencies, SBOMs, provenance, immutable CI dependencies, secret scanning, and blocking vulnerability gates.

## Compatibility

- Jellyfin: 10.11.3
- Jellyfin target ABI: 10.11.0.0
- File Transformation: optional fallback integration 2.5.3.0

## Upgrade note

Authentication and session-server destination now fail closed. Configure a strong Base64 JWT secret and explicitly select either a validated WebSocket URL or trusted same-host port 3000 auto-detection.
